title: Credit Access is Associated with Improved Food Security in the Horn of Africa
abstract: arXiv:2609.24382v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The intensification of climate change poses a growing threat to food security, especially in vulnerable communities. This study employs an observational machine-learning framework to estimate the causal association between access to credit and acute food insecurity in Somalia and across the Horn of Africa, drawing on a harmonized dataset spanning key environmental, socioeconomic, and conflict-related factors from 2015 to 2022. Results indicate that greater credit access is associated with a 2% reduction in acute food insecurity at the population level over the study period. Given that, on average, 16% of the population is in crisis, this effect represents a meaningful shift within the at-risk group. We interpret these estimates under explicit identification assumptions and complement them with robustness and refutation tests. translated_title: 信贷获取与非洲之角地区粮食安全的改善相关
translated_abstract: 气候变化的加剧对粮食安全构成日益严重的威胁，尤其是在脆弱社区。本研究采用观察性机器学习框架，基于2015年至2022年涵盖关键环境、社会经济和冲突相关因素的统一数据集，估计索马里及整个非洲之角地区信贷获取与急性粮食不安全之间的因果关联。结果表明，在研究期间，更高的信贷获取与人口层面上急性粮食不安全减少2%相关。鉴于平均有16%的人口处于危机状态，这一效应在风险群体中代表着有意义的转变。研究者在明确的识别假设下解释这些估计结果，并通过稳健性检验和反驳检验加以补充。这些结果为金融获取如何与粮食安全结果相关联提供了特定背景下的证据。
tldr: 本研究利用机器学习方法分析2015-2022年非洲之角数据，发现信贷获取的改善与急性粮食不安全减少2%相关，表明金融服务在缓解气候变化背景下的粮食危机中发挥着重要作用。
en_tdlr: Using an observational machine-learning framework on data from 2015-2022, this study finds that greater credit access is associated with a 2% reduction in acute food insecurity in the Horn of Africa, highlighting the meaningful role of financial access in mitigating food crises amid climate change.
